summary.en: A Pakistan-linked handler allegedly orchestrated a railway-track blast in Rajasthan that killed two people and led to two arrests, while a minibus-oil tanker collision in Punjab left nine dead and eleven injured. In Balochistan, a drone strike claimed by a separatist group killed six Pakistani military personnel, and a motorcycle bomb in Bara wounded two civilians. Saudi firms are pursuing a $30 billion energy investment in Pakistan and a Turkish drone order is prompting India to consider expanding its own production, while AI-generated audio falsely linked a Ghaziabad blast to Pakistan-linked proxies. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: En Pakistan-tilknyttet handler skal ha orkestrert en sprengning på jernbanespor i Rajasthan som drepte to personer og førte til to arrestasjoner, mens en kollisjon mellom minibus og oljetanker i Punjab drepte ni og såret elleve. I Balochistan drepte et droneram fra en separatistgruppe seks pakistanske militærpersonell, og en motorsykkelbombe i Bara såret to sivile. Saudiske firmaer forfølger en energiinvestering på 30 milliarder dollar i Pakistan, og en tyrkisk dronebestilling får India til å vurdere å utvide egen produksjon, mens AI-generert lyd feilaktig knyttet en eksplosjon i Ghaziabad til Pakistan-tilknyttede stedfortredere. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
